title: Design System: Submarine Museums of the World

display.purpose: Home title only; second line outlined, never filled.

headline.purpose: Inner page titles and section headlines.

title.purpose: Dossier names, rail titles, era plate names.

label.purpose: Codes, counts, years, ranges, field labels and table cells, set in IBM Plex Mono.

shadows.name: contact-glow
shadows.purpose: Live contact dot transmitting in its propulsion colour.

shadows.name: contact-ring
shadows.purpose: Quiet separation halo under a contact dot.

shadows.name: lock-glow
shadows.purpose: The single locked contact; alarm colour only.

shadows.name: selected-rule
shadows.purpose: Selected row in the contact log and register.

motion.name: ease-instrument
motion.purpose: Default state transition: colour, border, transform. 140–200ms.

motion.name: acquisition
motion.value: staggered contact adds + 120ms boot bar + 120ms entry bar
motion.purpose: The entry bar under the rail fills with the contact count while the boot terminal reports the link; both fade once the plot is complete.

motion.name: tactical-sheet
motion.purpose: Mobile filter board grows upward from the bottom bar.

motion.name: lock-ping
motion.purpose: Expanding ring on the locked contact.

motion.name: video-rotate
motion.purpose: Mobile player rotates 16:9 to fill the portrait screen; reset on close.

breakpoints.name: register
breakpoints.purpose: Register loses its sticky dossier and moves the file into a bottom sheet.

breakpoints.name: tactical
breakpoints.purpose: Tactical panel switches from bottom bar + sheet to an always-open four-column board.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Rail to 54px, single-column hero and dossier, full-screen video modal.

components.description: The single solid-green action: open the assigned file, open the register, apply the mission.

components.name: Line Button
components.description: Secondary action: open a dossier, open the playlist, dismiss.

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Propulsion filters carry a data dot; situation filters carry the archive's badge glyph. Both show a live count.

components.name: Contact Dot
components.description: A plotted submarine: 7px dot in its propulsion colour on a 30px hit area; red and pinged when locked.
components.css: .ds-contact { position:relative; display:grid; place-items:center; width:30px; height:30px; } .ds-contact i { width:7px; height:7px; border-radius:50%; background:var(--c,#e6f5eb); box-shadow:0 0 0 3px rgba(230,245,235,.08), 0 0 12px var(--c,#e6f5eb); transition:transform 180ms cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1); } .ds-contact:hover i { transform:scale(1.5); } .ds-contact.is-locked i { width:11px; height:11px; background:var(--alarm,#ff4d3d); box-shadow:0 0 0 4px rgba(255,77,61,.18), 0 0 22px rgba(255,77,61,.8); } .ds-contact.is-locked::after { content:''; position:absolute; inset:-12px; border:1px solid rgba(255,77,61,.5); border-radius:50%; }

components.name: Tactical Switch
components.description: A filter on the submarine board: square, hairline, a glowing data dot and a mono count. Pressed takes 13% of the data hue as ground and 60% as border.
components.css: .ds-switch { --c:var(--mut,#7d9487); display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:6px; min-height:38px; padding:0 9px; border:1px solid rgba(230,245,235,.13); background:rgba(4,8,6,.38); color:var(--dim,#93aa9d); font-family:var(--mono,monospace); font-size:8px; letter-spacing:.1em; text-transform:uppercase; white-space:nowrap; border-radius:0; cursor:pointer; transition:color 150ms cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1), border-color 150ms cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1), background 150ms cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1); } .ds-switch i { width:5px; height:5px; flex:none; border-radius:50%; background:var(--c); box-shadow:0 0 6px var(--c); opacity:.4; } .ds-switch b { font-weight:400; font-size:7px; color:var(--mut,#7d9487); } .ds-switch:hover { color:var(--txt,#e6f5eb); border-color:rgba(230,245,235,.32); } .ds-switch[aria-pressed="true"] { color:var(--txt,#e6f5eb); border-color:color-mix(in srgb, var(--c) 60%, transparent); background:color-mix(in srgb, var(--c) 13%, transparent); } .ds-switch[aria-pressed="true"] i { opacity:1; } .ds-switch[aria-pressed="true"] b { color:var(--txt,#e6f5eb); }

narrative.overview: The archive behaves like a confidential briefing built on a submarine plot: on arrival it assigns one preserved submarine, then opens its file. The map is the only control surface, framed by a tactical board of square switches with glowing data dots; phosphor green marks whatever is live, red marks the locked contact. The visual language is still the Acoustic Plot — green-black sea, cool phosphor readouts, heavy condensed uppercase, mono measurements — but it now lives in a bounded map section instead of a fixed backdrop, so the home reads as three decisive blocks: hero, map, detail. Light mode is a print of the same instrument on warm declassified stock, not a different brand. Nothing is decorated to look technical: the technical objects (codes, coordinates, years, counts) are the ornament.
keyCharacteristics: Three-block home: assigned mission, tactical plot, dossier of the target.
One assignment per visit, echoed as MISSION TARGET in the detail block.
Map as the only filter surface: bottom tactical panel on mobile, four-column board on desktop.
Two printed states from the same tokens: phosphor CRT plot (default) and DECLASSIFIED PAPER.
Archivo condensed display plus IBM Plex Mono data labels; no third face.
Zero radius, one-pixel hairlines, tonal elevation instead of shadows.
Every count is generated from the JSON snapshot at runtime.
Static scanlines on the dark plot only; the paper theme and data hues stay clean.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Phosphor green appears on ≤10% of any screen and always marks something alive or selected. If phosphor green is already spent, use type weight or a hairline.

rules.name: The Encoding Rule
rules.body: A colour that encodes data (propulsion, situation) never becomes a surface colour. It may appear as a dot, a badge, a border tint, a bar or text — never as a panel background.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: Light mode is a print of the same instrument, not a different brand. Every surface, hairline and data hue must remain legible in both themes; never hard-code a dark colour on a themed surface.

rules.name: The Measurement Rule
rules.body: Mono is for anything the instrument would measure or name: codes, years, counts, ranges, coordinates, labels, table cells. Running prose and headings are always Archivo.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface never gains a shadow to look important. If it must separate from the plot, it gains a hairline, a tonal step, or blur — never a cast shadow.

rules.name: The Glow-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Halos exist only where something is transmitting: contacts, locks, the live indicator. A halo on a button or a card is a bug.

rules.name: The CRT Rule
rules.body: CRT effects belong to the dark map, not the interface: static scanlines at low opacity, no flicker, no moving lines, no global green filter. Data hues and the paper theme remain untouched.

dos: Do assign a destination on arrival and let the detail block answer it.
Do keep the map as the only filter surface; every control is reachable from the tactical panel.
Do reserve phosphor green for live data and selection, and red for the single locked contact.
Do test both themes on every surface, especially sheets and media wells.
Do set every code, count, year and range in mono with 0.10em+ tracking.
Do generate every number from the JSON snapshot at runtime.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion by removing the ping, the acquisition sequence and the reveals.
donts: Don't add border-radius to surfaces or buttons; only data marks are round.
Don't add drop shadows to cards, panels or buttons.
Don't use phosphor green or red as a surface fill beyond the primary button and the lock tint.
Don't hard-code dark colours inside themed components; use --panel, --ink-*, --line and --txt.
Don't use mono for running prose, or Archivo for measurements.
Don't put a coloured left/right border thicker than 1px on cards or callouts.
Don't animate layout properties, or animate anything that is not a state change, the acquisition sequence or the plot.
Don't add flicker, moving scanlines or a global green filter; CRT is the map's ground, not a filter over data.
